propositions: On platforms without /proc (e.g. macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing dead processes with recycled pids to be judged incorrectly as live, creating unbounded lock wedges.

When current_start is None (unqualified liveness verdict), _mkdir_lock_is_stale must fall back to the _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S backstop instead of returning False, ensuring orphaned locks are bounded by the 1-hour ceiling.

Live owners holding both fcntl and mkdir legs cannot reach _mkdir_lock_is_stale while holding their lock (precondition of _acquire_mkdir), so ceiling-based reclamation can only fire on orphans and cannot break genuinely-live owners.
The lock.py module (798 LOC) was split along call-graph seams into lock.py (~510 LOC) and lock_owner.py (~339 LOC) to stay within the 200–800 LOC module-size limit while fixing the defect.

All 12 monkeypatch string-form references and 42 attribute-access references to moved functions must be repointed to lock_owner without re-export shims to ensure patch sites are load-bearing and not silently bypassed.
